title: Change Summary Into Analysis
author: Chee Skool
instruction: Revise this summary-only idea into two or three analytical sentences: one source gives a redevelopment proposal and several projected benefits. Explain what makes the source's support convincing or limited compared with the other source.
sourceFocus: Use one concrete detail from the market-block sources and explain how it affects the strength of the argument.
successCriteria: Includes at least one specific source detail instead of only describing the topic.
Explains why the detail affects the argument's strength.
Makes a comparison or evaluation rather than retelling both sources.
Keeps the claim within the evidence actually provided.
modelResponse: Source B is more convincing because it connects its redevelopment recommendation to specific site constraints and a staged plan rather than only listing expected benefits. That evidence gives the reader a way to judge whether the proposal can work on this block, while the broader projections in Source A depend more heavily on assumptions that have not yet been demonstrated.
revisionPrompts: If I removed the phrase 'this matters because,' would my reasoning still be visible?
Am I evaluating the evidence, or only telling the reader what each source says?
authoringNotes: The learner revises a deliberately vague summary frame into comparative analysis.
